title: A rerun finds its spec by content, and a loose ticket by its spec

statements.says: tracker-publish can be run again after a run that failed on the network, and it must find what that run filed rather than file it twice.
With github, a spec is found again by a hash of its title and its body, written in a hidden HTML comment on the first line of the body.
A rerun with the same spec file finds its own issue.
A spec with the same title and a different body gets an issue of its own, and the command says which open spec shares its title.
A ticket is still found by its title among its spec's sub-issues.
A ticket carries its spec's number in a hidden comment on its first line, and a rerun matches a loose ticket by its title and that number.
The hidden lines stay in every issue the command files.
The format of the hidden lines is held as it is.
An issue with no hidden line is not matched by its title, so a rerun that spans the change files once more, one time only.
A failed run may have made the issue and never heard its number back, so the rerun needs something it knows before it files.
In the retest of 4 October a Grill published a spec whose title matched an older open spec, the command matched by title and returned the old number, and the driver ran the old design.
The driver does not close a spec when a run ends, so an old spec can wait open a long time for a new one to share its title.
Two Grills that pick one title at about the same time meet the same fault, and the second spec is lost with no error.
A ticket filed before a failed link has no parent yet.
What a loose ticket lacks is which spec it serves, not its content.
A change to the hidden lines' format means the issues filed before it no longer match.
Matching a spec by its title was rejected, because it is the fault the retest of 4 October showed.
Keeping the hash in a label was rejected, because a label holds 50 characters and a sha256 hash needs 64.
Keeping the hash in a comment on the issue was rejected, because it is a second call after the issue is made, so a failure between the two leaves an issue a rerun cannot find.
Hashing each ticket as well was rejected, because Gap and rename tickets hold text a fresh Session writes on each run, so a hash would never match and each rerun would leave a stray open ticket.
Falling back to the title for an issue with no hidden line was rejected, because every open spec filed before the change would keep the fault.
